newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge turns down Ajinomoto plea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge turns down Ajinomoto plea.

text.p: A U.S. district court judge on Friday declined to accept a no contest plea from Ajinomoto Co of Japan in a price-fixing case in the United States involving lysine, a feed additive.
Judge Ruben Castillo of the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois said he was concerned that Ajinomoto's no contest plea did not reflect the severity of the anti-trust charges.
Under an agreement reached in August with the U.S. Justice Department, Ajinomoto had agreed to plead no contest.
Ajinomoto now has four weeks to decide if it will plead guilty before its agreement with Justice expires.
"I am deeply troubled by the reaction of this company (Ajinomoto)," Castillo said at a court hearing.
An attorney for Ajinomoto admitted that the Japanese company had started to shred documents related to the lysine price-fixing case soon after the Justice probe became known.
The judge did accept guilty pleas on price-fixing in the lysine case from Kyowa Hakko Kogyo of Japan and Sewon Co Ltd of Korea.

The three foreign firms were accused of fixing prices as part of a Justice probe of the lysine market. That investigation targeted Archer Daniels Midland Co, which this week pleaded guilty to fixing lysine prices and agreed to pay a $70 million fine.

ADM also pleaded guilty to fixing prices of citric acid, which is used in food, beverages and other products, and to pay a $30 million fine. Justice officials have said ADM is cooperating in an ongoing probe of the citric acid market.
ADM was also granted immunity for cooperating in an ongoing investigation of possible price-fixing of high fructose corn syrup, Justice said this week.
